title: Microeconomist: continuous batching recommendation pipeline (SLO-aware heuristics & safe apply)
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Build a continuous recommendation engine (Microeconomist) that synthesizes batching and caching configuration suggestions per workload while guaranteeing SLO-safe applies and automated rollback. The system uses lightweight per-workload microeconometric models to trade latency, cost, and token-efficiency signals and emits ranked recommended parameter sets (microbatch size, kv-window, prefix-caching TTL, model-variant fallback rules).

Scope:
- Telemetry + profiler: collect per-route sequence length distribution, cold/hot KV cache hit rates, token latency P50/P95, and per-token cost estimates over sliding windows.
- Heuristics & scoring: implement SLO-aware scoring that penalizes recommendations likely to violate latency SLOs, and prioritize configs that reduce estimated token cost by >3% with high confidence.
- Continuous apply: propose a shadow-apply -> canary -> gradual rollout pipeline with automatic rollback thresholds and safety gates (latency regressions, error spikes, SLA violations).
- Simulation sandbox: a synthetic replay runner to simulate recommended config impact using historical traces before any production apply.
- Operator UI: lightweight Console page with recommended sets, rationale, expected savings, risk score, and one-click guarded apply options.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Conservative vs aggressive savings: initially bias towards conservative savings (smaller microbatch increases, short TTL cache suggestions) to build trust, then expose more aggressive profiles as the model proves stable.
- Compute for profiling: prefer streaming lightweight summaries over full-length traces to conserve telemetry ingestion costs.
- Complexity of model: start with linear microeconomic model (cost per token vs latency penalty) and add Bayesian uncertainty estimates for confidence scoring rather than heavy ML models for first iteration.

Acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end pipeline that generates recommendations for 95% of production routes with valid telemetry.
2) Shadow-sim replay accuracy: simulated cost savings estimate within +/- 8% of measured savings from a controlled canary.
3) Safe apply mechanics: automated rollback triggers on >10% P95 latency regression or >1.5x error-rate multiplier within the rollout window.
4) Console integration: recommendations visible in Console with rationale and risk score; operator can start a guarded rollout from the UI.
5) Documentation and runbook for on-call and SRE with rollback/playbook steps.

Longer-term notes: add multi-armed bandit style experiments to choose between competing config families, and add cross-workload coordination to avoid cluster-level oscillations.
acceptance_criteria: Generate recommendations for >=95% of active production routes using available telemetry
Shadow-simulation cost estimate within +/-8% vs controlled canary measurement

implementation_notes: Use rolling 1-min windows for telemetry aggregation; compute sequence-length percentiles and KV hit-rate per bucket
Scoring function = estimated_cost_savings * confidence - alpha * predicted_p95_regression where alpha is tunable per-customer tier
Shadow-sim should emulate both KV-cold and KV-warm starts; add synthetic warmup steps based on observed churn rates
Rollout protocol: shadow -> canary(1%) -> ramp(1,5,10,25,50) with minimum 30-min observation windows unless statistically overridden
Rollback: immediate if P95 latency > baseline*1.10 for two consecutive windows or error-rate > 1.5x for single window
